item.text: {"text":"HSTU’s original paper establishes the sequential transducer backbone, but does not establish that title/description semantics learned from scratch improve sparse-item recommendation. Nearby work emphasizes aligning textual and behavioral representations: ST2SI (2025) explicitly models item transitions and addresses text–ID misalignment; LETTER (2025) combines textual and collaborative information through semantic codes and masked alignment objectives. These support interaction-grounded semantics rather than treating lexical similarity as compatibility. Neither establishes the requested from-scratch HSTU recipe. Sources: [HSTU](https://arxiv.org/abs/2402.17152), [ST2SI](https://aclanthology.org/2025.coling-main.171/), [LETTER](https://arxiv.org/abs/2503.12183).\n\nA 2026 preprint, SISA-Rec, combines gated ID/text fusion with ranking and contrastive alignment, but uses BERT text embeddings; its reported gains therefore do not validate training without pretrained weights. Transferable experimental hypothesis: retain one HSTU and represent each item as an ID embedding plus a gated lexical residual from a randomly initialized, jointly trained title/description encoder. Preserve alphanumeric model identifiers and local word order to distinguish product versions, intended uses and content experiences; supervise the shared representation through next-item prediction, optionally with a lightly weighted text–ID alignment loss. These are proposed adaptations, not demonstrated findings from the cited papers. Interactions must determine whether shared wording predicts substitutes, complements or unrelated items; titles alone cannot establish compatibility. Compare against the corrected ID-only baseline using the fixed macro validation HR@10, including sparse-item diagnostics. Source: [SISA-Rec](https://arxiv.org/abs/2607.11168)."}
